# frostjs

> A deny-by-default capability linter for JavaScript. A one-screen policy says which browser capabilities the code may use (storage, network destinations, code generation, HTML injection, identity, navigation, globals, workers); the build fails on anything else, naming the file, line, expression and policy line. Built for pipelines where an AI assistant writes code.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): value proposition, two-minute setup, the policy grammar, every capability code, and a block to paste into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md so an assistant respects the gate.
- [SHOWCASE](SHOWCASE.md): what it found in three.js 0.160.0 (a URL-parameter-gated remote eval, and a runtime import from a CDN).
- [ARCHITECTURE](ARCHITECTURE.md): the pipeline, the contract a recognizer signs, the invariants.
- [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md): the zero-false-positive rule and how the corpus enforces it.
- [AGENTS](AGENTS.md): instructions for AI agents changing this repository.
- [SECURITY](SECURITY.md): what a green run promises, what it does not, how to report a bypass.

## Commands

After `npm install -D @keithadler/frostjs` (the npm name is scoped; the command is `frostjs`):

- `npx frostjs init src`: write a starter policy from what the code does today.
- `npx frostjs src`: check; exit 1 on a denial.
- `npx frostjs summary`: the policy in plain English.
- `npx frostjs csp`: the Content-Security-Policy header the policy implies.
- `npx frostjs vendor add <file>`, `npx frostjs registry sync`, `npx frostjs sri`: third-party code by fingerprint.

## Policy grammar

```
policy "<name>"
ignore "<glob>", ...
vendored "<glob>", ...
may use <capability> [in "<glob>", ...] [until YYYY-MM-DD]   -- hint
may reach "<host>", ... [in "<glob>", ...] [until YYYY-MM-DD]
forbid [using] <capability> [in "<glob>", ...]
forbid reaching "<host>", ...
```
